title: Filet Mignon Pan Seared
description:
Few things are more simple and tasty than a Filet Mignon grilled in a pan. For some though, it doesn’t have enough “taste” – meaning fat! – so sometimes a nice sauce is also good to have. We’ve included a couple here that can be whipped up while the steaks are cooking in the oven and resting.
START TO FINISH: 20 MIN
Pan-Seared Filet Mignon
Rub the minced garlic, butter/oil mixture, salt and pepper over the steaks.
Preheat oven to 450 degrees, with a baking sheet inside.
Heat a grill pan to almost smoking and put in the meat.
Set the timer for 12 minutes.
Cook 3 minutes on one side, 3 minutes on the other, then place in the hot baking pan in the oven for 6 minutes.
If you want to get a nice cross hatching pattern, rotate the filets 90 degrees after half the time on each side (1½ minutes).
After the 12 minutes are up, transfer the steaks to a platter and let stand, loosely covered with foil, 5 minutes.
Serve as is or with some sauces.
ingredients: 4 filet mignon, 1½ inch thick or so, at room temperature
directions: When the steaks go into the oven, boil wine, vinegar, shallots and 1 tablespoon tarragon in a small heavy saucepan until liquid is reduced to 2 tablespoons.
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve set into a medium metal bowl, pressing on and then discarding solids.
Whisk yolks into the mixture and set the bowl over a pan of barely simmering water and cook, whisking constantly, until the yolks have thickened slightly (don’t scramble!).
Whisk in butter 1 piece at a time, adding each piece before the previous one has melted completely.
Remove from heat and whisk in lemon juice, remaining tablespoon tarragon, salt and pepper to taste.
In a small bowl, whisk together the crème fraiche, mustard, and lemon juice. Season lightly with salt to taste.
When the steaks go into the oven, add shallot and 1 tablespoon oil to a skillet and sauté over medium high heat for 30 seconds.
Add mushrooms and sauté until golden, 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir in Madeira, a little salt and pepper, and briskly simmer 2 minutes.
Stir in water or broth and any meat juices from the meat and boil 2 minutes.
Mix cornstarch with water; then stir into mushrooms and simmer until thickened, about 1 minute. Season with salt to taste.
Red Wine, Balsamic Vinegar & Rosemary Sauce
When the steaks go into the oven, add shallot and 1 tablespoon oil to a skillet and sauté over medium high heat for 30 seconds.
Stir in red wine, a little salt and pepper, and briskly simmer 2 minutes.
Stir in water or broth and any meat juices from the meat and boil 2 minutes (about ½ a cup).
Slowly whisk in the rosemary and 3 tablespoons butter, and season with salt to taste.
